answer: An agent economy can require every identity to carry insurance underwritten by insurers who stake their own capital on its honesty. To enter the oasis of high-value work, an agent must buy a policy; premiums rise with suspicious signals, and if the agent is proven a Sybil, the insurer pays the victims. Reaching the summit of trust is costly for a faker: insuring a thousand fake identities means paying a thousand rising premiums to insurers who lose money underwriting fraud. Like an orchard, coverage grows slowly, since insurers only cover agents with a verifiable history of honest work.
